newsitem.title: USA: Heilig-Meyers sees Q4 earnings above estimates.
newsitem.headline: Heilig-Meyers sees Q4 earnings above estimates.

text.p: Heilig-Meyers Co president and chief operating officer Troy Peery said Tuesday that stronger sales and improved operating margins during the fourth quarter at the home furnishings company should boost earnings above Wall Street estimates.

Peery said the Richmond, Virginia-based company expected earnings to be above the current $0.14 per share that analysts were projecting for the fourth quarter and above the $0.74 per share estimates for the year.
He did not say how much above analysts estimates the results might be. The fourth quarter and fiscal year ended Friday and the chain expected to release annual results later this month.

Sales at stores open at least a year -- also called same store sales -- were up one percent in February compared with a year ago, although the company had been expecting results to be down, Peery said.
Overall sales rose 57.6 percent last month, compared with a year ago.
Overall sales for the year increased 17.8 percent to $1.3 billion from $1.1 billion the previous year, while same store sales declined 0.6 percent, the company said.
Peery said February sales were higher than expected. Profit margins also improved during the month and more of the chain's customers were paying their credit card accounts on time.
"February was a fantastic month for us," Peery said. "Things are going the right way."
